item.title: Free Diapers, Baby Food Distribution Set for Milton Wednesday
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: State Representative Michelle Salzman is partnering with The Cutting Board and community organizers to distribute free diapers and baby food to Santa Rosa County families still recovering from Hurricane Isaias. The event is scheduled for Wednesday, October 28, from 4 to 6 p.m. at The Cutting Board, 8855 FL-87 in Milton. Farm Share will supply an…
item.content:encoded:
State Representative Michelle Salzman is partnering with The Cutting Board and community organizers to distribute free diapers and baby food to Santa Rosa County families still recovering from Hurricane Isaias. The event is scheduled for Wednesday, October 28, from 4 to 6 p.m. at The Cutting Board, 8855 FL-87 in Milton.

Farm Share will supply an estimated 1,500 diapers in sizes 1, 3, and 5, plus 10 pallets of Beech-Nut baby food pouches. According to the press release, the distribution aims to help families access everyday necessities during the ongoing storm recovery period. "One of the things I love most about our community is how people come together when times get tough," Salzman said in a statement. "We want to be part of that kindness by helping local families with diapers and baby food and reminding them that they haven't been forgotten."

The Cutting Board owner Nan Foster emphasized that diapers and baby food are essential supplies during crisis recovery. "When a storm impacts our community, families with little ones face challenges that many people may not immediately think about," Foster said. Federal and state constituent services representatives will be on-site to connect families with additional resources. The event is open to the public, and free treats will be provided while supplies last.

item.content:encoded:
At least three people were killed in a fiery vehicle crash overnight in Pensacola at the intersection of Cervantes and M Street, according to Pensacola Police.

The crash occurred when a vehicle traveling eastbound on Cervantes Street struck a barrier at M Street and became engulfed in flames. Multiple occupants were in the vehicle at the time of impact.

Pensacola Police responded to the scene. No additional details about the victims, the cause of the crash, or ongoing investigation have been released at this time.

item.title: Sunny Skies, Upper 70s Expected Through Early Week in Pensacola
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A sprawling high pressure system is settling over the North Escambia area this weekend, bringing classic fall weather that locals have been waiting for. Expect mostly sunny skies and dry conditions through Monday, with afternoon highs climbing to the mid-to-upper 70s—ideal for outdoor activities and weekend plans. Nights will turn crisp as…
item.content:encoded:
A sprawling high pressure system is settling over the North Escambia area this weekend, bringing classic fall weather that locals have been waiting for. Expect mostly sunny skies and dry conditions through Monday, with afternoon highs climbing to the mid-to-upper 70s—ideal for outdoor activities and weekend plans.

Nights will turn crisp as temperatures drop, typical for late October in Northwest Florida. The ridge of high pressure anchoring overhead should keep rain chances essentially zero through the weekend and into early next week, making this an excellent stretch for anyone looking to get outside without worrying about unexpected showers.

If you're planning any outdoor events or yard work around Pensacola, this is your window. The pattern looks stable, so don't expect any weather surprises to disrupt your Saturday or Sunday.

item.content:encoded: The Northview Chiefs fought hard Friday night but couldn't get past the Baker Gators in a district football game at Tommy Weaver Memorial Stadium in Bratt, falling 41-28. Despite the loss, the Chiefs stayed competitive throughout the contest, showing resilience in a game that came down to execution in the final moments. The Gators' offense proved too much to contain in the second half as Baker pulled away to secure the district victory. Northview will look to bounce back in their next district outing as the season enters the home stretch.

item.content:encoded: The Pace Patriots spoiled Tate's homecoming celebration Friday night, dominating the Aggies 29-12 in a district matchup at Pete Gindl Stadium in Cantonment. The decisive victory extended Pace's recent stranglehold on the rivalry to eight consecutive wins over Tate. Despite the festive atmosphere surrounding the homecoming event, the Aggies couldn't muster enough offense to keep pace with the visiting Patriots, who pulled away decisively in the second half. The loss leaves Tate looking to bounce back in its remaining regular-season games.

item.content:encoded: A mobile museum celebrating the United States' 250th anniversary has arrived in Creola, Alabama, offering visitors an interactive look at the nation's founding history. item.title: Escambia County Government Meetings Set for Oct. 26-30
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County and affiliated boards have scheduled several public meetings for the coming week, with most activity concentrated on Wednesday. Monday's agenda includes a WFPL Board of Governance Meeting at 4 p.m. at Tryon Library on Langley Avenue. Tuesday brings the Pensacola-Escambia Promotion and Development Commission Board Meeting at 10 a.m.…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County and affiliated boards have scheduled several public meetings for the coming week, with most activity concentrated on Wednesday.

Monday's agenda includes a WFPL Board of Governance Meeting at 4 p.m. at Tryon Library on Langley Avenue. Tuesday brings the Pensacola-Escambia Promotion and Development Commission Board Meeting at 10 a.m. at CO:LAB on West Garden Street; an Environmental Enforcement Special Magistrate Hearing scheduled for 1:30 p.m. has been canceled.

Wednesday is the busiest day. The Affordable Housing Advisory Committee meets at 9 a.m., followed by the Escambia Children's Trust Board at the same time in the Ernie Lee Magaha Government Building on Palafox Place. The Development Review Committee convenes at 1 p.m., and the Visit Pensacola Board of Directors meets at 3 p.m. at 120 Church St. The Santa Rosa Island Authority Board will meet at 5 p.m. at their office on Via de Luna Drive in Pensacola Beach. An Audit Committee meeting for the FloridaWest Economic Development Alliance, also scheduled for 3 p.m., has been canceled.

Thursday and Friday have no meetings scheduled. Most county meetings can be streamed live or accessed later through MyEscambia.com/ectv, YouTube, and local cable channels. Anyone needing accommodations under the Americans with Disabilities Act should contact Human Resources at 850-595-3279.

item.title: Gulf Shores pop-up festival gives Shrimp Festival vendors a second chance
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: More than two weeks after the National Shrimp Festival's cancellation, some of the vendors and artists who were counting on the event are getting another opportunity to sell their work and recover losses. According to WKRG News 5, a pop-up festival in Gulf Shores is now offering participating artists and craftspeople a chance to showcase their…
item.content:encoded:
More than two weeks after the National Shrimp Festival's cancellation, some of the vendors and artists who were counting on the event are getting another opportunity to sell their work and recover losses.

According to WKRG News 5, a pop-up festival in Gulf Shores is now offering participating artists and craftspeople a chance to showcase their talents after the 53rd annual National Shrimp Festival was called off.

The cancellation left many vendors facing significant financial losses after preparing inventory and making travel arrangements for what is typically one of the Gulf Coast's largest annual events. The pop-up festival represents a lifeline for those looking to recoup some of those losses before the busy holiday shopping season.

Details about the timing, location, and participating vendors at the pop-up event were not immediately available.

item.title: Escambia school board members ordered to sit for depositions in book challenge lawsuit
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A court has ruled that Escambia County School Board members must submit to depositions in an ongoing lawsuit over book removals from school libraries, according to reporting from Courthouse News cited by the civil rights group Protect Democracy. The order comes after school board members had sought to avoid answering questions under oath about…
item.content:encoded:
A court has ruled that Escambia County School Board members must submit to depositions in an ongoing lawsuit over book removals from school libraries, according to reporting from Courthouse News cited by the civil rights group Protect Democracy.

The order comes after school board members had sought to avoid answering questions under oath about their decisions to ban certain books, while simultaneously requesting that students affected by the case be deposed instead. A judge has now rejected that approach, requiring the board members themselves to provide sworn testimony about the rationale behind the library book challenges.

The case centers on efforts by parents and advocacy groups challenging the removal of books from Escambia County schools. Book challenges in the district have been a contentious issue in recent years, with disputes over age-appropriate content and parental rights in school libraries.

The ruling marks a legal setback for the school board's litigation strategy and could lead to significant testimony about how removal decisions were made.

item.title: Taddeo hosts Pensacola insurance roundtable with GOP primary rival
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Democratic candidate for Florida Chief Financial Officer Annette Taddeo will host a roundtable discussion Monday morning in Pensacola focused on the state's ongoing insurance crisis, bringing together insurance experts and a notable political ally: Dr. Frank Collige, a former Republican primary candidate for the same CFO position who is now…
item.content:encoded:
Democratic candidate for Florida Chief Financial Officer Annette Taddeo will host a roundtable discussion Monday morning in Pensacola focused on the state's ongoing insurance crisis, bringing together insurance experts and a notable political ally: Dr. Frank Collige, a former Republican primary candidate for the same CFO position who is now backing Taddeo's campaign.

The roundtable, scheduled for 9 a.m. Monday at Rafferty Domnick Cunningham & Yaffa on South Palafox Street, will examine rising homeowners insurance premiums, transparency in the insurance industry, and consumer protections. Collige received more than 610,000 votes in the Republican primary but has since endorsed Taddeo, citing shared concerns about insurance reform despite their different party affiliations.

"Florida homeowners cannot afford another four years of partisan politics while their insurance bills keep climbing," Taddeo said in a statement. "The next CFO must be an independent watchdog, not another political loyalist." Collige echoed that sentiment, saying the two may disagree on some issues but share views on what needs to change in Florida's insurance system.

The discussion will also feature Gary Rosen, president of the National Association of Environmentally Responsible Mold Contractors. Taddeo is running on a platform centered on affordability, accountability, and anti-corruption. The roundtable is open to media coverage.

item.title: West Highway 4 Resurfacing Work Begins; 13-Mile Project Set to Run Through Spring
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Construction crews have begun work on a major resurfacing and improvement project on West Highway 4, with C.W. Roberts Contracting starting operations on Monday, Oct. 19. The 13-mile project will address deteriorating road base and asphalt while also replacing worn guardrails along the route. According to Escambia County Community and Media…
item.content:encoded:
Construction crews have begun work on a major resurfacing and improvement project on West Highway 4, with C.W. Roberts Contracting starting operations on Monday, Oct. 19. The 13-mile project will address deteriorating road base and asphalt while also replacing worn guardrails along the route.

According to Escambia County Community and Media Relations, the work involves milling operations to remove excess asphalt, repairing cracked layers, correcting base layer issues, and applying new asphalt in two stages to improve drainage and road longevity. Contractors plan to work in 2-3 mile segments to keep disruption manageable for regular commuters.

The full scope of improvements includes addressing the road slope for better water drainage and installing new guardrails in deteriorated sections. Weather and construction coordination will factor into the timeline, but county officials expect the project to wrap up by spring 2027. Escambia County is asking drivers to be patient as work continues.

item.content:encoded:
The Republic of Korea Ship Hansando will arrive at Naval Air Station Pensacola on Sunday, Oct. 26, according to a media advisory from NAS Pensacola.

The visit marks a stop for the South Korean vessel as part of ongoing international naval operations and cooperation efforts in the region. NAS Pensacola regularly hosts foreign military ships as part of joint training exercises and diplomatic visits.

Details on public access, tour availability, or specific timing for the ship's arrival were not included in the initial announcement. Those seeking more information are encouraged to contact NAS Pensacola's public affairs office.
